550: 			JCStatement assign = maker.Exec(maker.Assign(fieldInThis, rhs));
551: 			
552: 			// In case of @Builder.Default, set the value to the default if it was not set in the builder.

563: 			if (hasNonNullAnnotations(bfd.originalFieldNode)) {

569: 		List<JCAnnotation> annsOnMethod = job.checkerFramework.generateSideEffectFree() ? List.of(maker.Annotation(genTypeRef(job.parentType, CheckerFrameworkVersion.NAME__SIDE_EFFECT_FREE), List.<JCExpression>nil())) : List.<JCAnnotation>nil();

575: 		// First add all generics that are present on the parent type.
576: 		ListBuffer<JCExpression> typeParamsForBuilderParameter = getTypeParamExpressions(job.typeParams, maker, job.sourceNode);
577: 		// Now add the <?, ?>.
578: 		JCWildcard wildcard = maker.Wildcard(maker.TypeBoundKind(BoundKind.UNBOUND), null);
579: 		typeParamsForBuilderParameter.append(wildcard);
580: 		wildcard = maker.Wildcard(maker.TypeBoundKind(BoundKind.UNBOUND), null);
581: 		typeParamsForBuilderParameter.append(wildcard);

The fix is complete and validated. 

**Root cause:** `@SuperBuilder`'s javadoc support in both backends read the doc comment from the wrong node:
- **javac** (`src/core/lombok/javac/handlers/HandleSuperBuilder.java`): when generating builder setters, the handler read the javadoc from the *newly generated builder field* (which has none) instead of the original annotated field, so setters got empty javadoc and `@param` lines were never moved off the original fields. Fixed by using `originalFieldNode` for the doc comment source and the cleanup task (src/core/lombok/javac/handlers/HandleSuperBuilder.java:1156).
- **Eclipse** (`src/core/lombok/eclipse/handlers/HandleSuperBuilder.java`): no javadoc copying existed at all. Added `copyJavadoc(originalFieldNode, setter, td, CopyJavadoc.SETTER, returnStatement != null)`, mirroring what `HandleBuilder` does for `@Builder` (src/core/lombok/eclipse/handlers/HandleSuperBuilder.java:1014).
